name: Ge Hong medical text in the Daoist Canon
description: A medical text attributed to Ge Hong and containing a Qinghao reference survives in the 1445 Daoist Canon.

impact.note: One surviving copy of an older text, changing nothing itself, though its qinghao passage later informed the artemisinin work.

date.basis: Date applies to the scoped observation or event; it is not a claim of global origin.

events.statement: A medical text attributed to Ge Hong and containing a Qinghao reference survives in the 1445 Daoist Canon.

evidence.locator: Textual history and discussion of the Daoist Canon
evidence.supports: The dissertation discusses Ge Hong’s fourth-century medical text, later revision and its preservation in the 1445 Daoist Canon. The surviving witness cannot be assumed to reproduce fourth-century wording without change; the cited chapter includes a reference to Qinghao.

events.caveats: The 1445 date refers to a surviving textual witness. Ge Hong worked in the fourth century, but later revision means the exact original wording and reception cannot be presumed. This historical text is not modern artemisinin treatment.
